integrity: The unique-response condition forces the strong vertices to form a 2-packing. In a crown graph such a packing has size at most two, and every two-vertex packing is one deleted matched pair. Each of the cases with zero, one, or two strong vertices then has completely forced labels, yielding the full enumerator and the minimum classification.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns unique-response strong Roman domination, while the scalar ordinary strong Roman crown value is prior work.
Finite exhaustive verification covers n=3,4,5 and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed crown treatment may exist.
title: All unique-response strong Roman functions of crown graphs
